answer: A mesa of trust works like this: a new agent starts on the flat top with nothing to spend, and every useful job it completes adds one step up a spiral staircase of reputation that takes weeks of verified work to climb. Attackers face a nebula of cost: each fake identity must separately climb the same slow spiral, paying compute and stake at every step, while clusters that vouch for each other get audited together and lose their deposits. Cloning is therefore expensive, slow, and self-exposing.
